data.command: What security tools do you have deployed?

data.text:
We've got a few security tools up our sleeve. We're running Ubuntu 22.04.3 LTS, and I've got a few services running in the background to keep things safe.

First off, we've got a Next-Generation Firewall (NGFW) running on the system, which is configured to block suspicious traffic. It's a pretty standard setup, but I'm running the latest version of UFW (Uncomplicated Firewall), which is versioned at 0.40, on top of the Ubuntu 22.04.3 LTS kernel 5.15.0-91. UFW is configured to deny all incoming traffic by default, but we've opened up port 443 for HTTPS traffic to our web server, as well as port 80 for HTTP traffic.

We're also running a few security-related services in the background. We've got Fail2Ban configured to monitor log files for signs of brute-force attacks, and to lock out IP addresses that try to login too many times. It's version 0.11.5. We've also got Snort IDS running on the system, which is a network traffic analyzer that can detect and prevent malicious activity. It's version 2.9.9.
